sources.citation: Mahato, Umapada. 2024. Kurmali Bhasha aur Hindi Bhasha ka tulnatmak adhyayan. PhD thesis, University Dept. of Hindi, Vinoba Bhave University, Hazaribagh (Shodhganga hdl 10603/540040). Contents + ch. 5 'Dhvani vigyan ke adhar par tulna' (pp. 142-181), scanned (Kruti Dev font).
sources.note: No Kurmali-specific statement. बलाघात 'stress' occurs once (p. 143) inside a quoted textbook definition of phonemics listing suprasegmentals in general; the chapter otherwise compares letters/sounds, vowel matras (only short i/u written in Kurmali), script conventions and dialect geography.

sources.citation: Gautam, Bhim Lal & Sharada Sapkota. 2024. Shifting identity in Kurmali: a preliminary observation. Nepalese Linguistics 38(1): 30-39. doi:10.3126/nl.v38i1.71551.
Khalid, Zoya. 2024. A Descriptive Grammar of Kurmali (JNU PhD): remaining bitstreams 04_abstract, 09_chapter5-11_chapter7, 12_annexures.
sources.note: Completeness only: chapters 5-7 are NP/VP/syntax; a stray remark on emphatic clitics/focus prosody is possible but no word-stress rule expected. download requires cookie+Referer trick (plain GET redirects to unreachable port 8443).

sources.citation: Khalid, Zoya. 2024. A Descriptive Grammar of Kurmali. PhD thesis, Centre for Linguistics, Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi (Shodhganga hdl 10603/704633). Ch. 3 'Kurmali Phonology', pp. 45-79; also title page, contents, ch. 1 (intro/methodology), ch. 2 (lit. review), ch. 4 (morphological processes).
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 3 sections: 3.1 consonants (minimal pairs, distribution, l~r, clusters, gemination), 3.2 vowels (six-vowel 'Oriya type' system; 3.2.4 'Vowel length is not phonemic in Kurmali'; 3.2.5 nasalisation 'usually not phonemic'; ablaut; elision), 3.3 syllable structure (C)V(V)(C)(C). No stress/accent/prosody/intonation section; the words 'stress'/'accent' occur only in a Masica quote about geminates (p. 66) and a generic clitic definition (ch. 4 p. 80).

sources.citation: Jana, Susnata. 2023. Kudmali Bhasha O Sanskriti; and Mahato, Kiriti & Bishwanath Mahato (eds.) 2023. Kudmali Bhasha O Sanskriti vol. 2. In Bengali; archive.org.
sources.note: Silent (culture, vocabulary, folk-etymological speculation on pronouns); no stress terms.

sources.citation: Language Division, ORGI. 2023. Linguistic Survey of India: Jharkhand. 'Panch Pargania' chapter (closely related/trade variety; LSI-Bihar equates Kurmali-as-trade-language with Panchpargania).
sources.note: Silent; 2.1.2 'Supra segmental phonemes' lists only vowel nasalization. (Not the target variety; checked for context only.)

sources.citation: Mahato, Kshudiram. 1380 BS [1973], reprint 2023. Kudmali Bhashatattwa [কুড়মালি ভাষাতত্ত্ব]. Purulia. 48 pp. In Bengali (= Glottolog ref 556501).
sources.note: Silent; historical/areal essay plus verb paradigms, vocabulary and song texts; no ধ্বনিতত্ত্ব section, no শ্বাসাঘাত/ঝোঁক.

sources.citation: 'Kurmali language and culture' (Manbhum-Purulia). IMPACT: IJRHAL 10(2), Feb 2022.
Singh, Gyaneshwar. 2022. Historical Perspective of Kurmali Language. Ranchi (self-published); archive.org.
Ghosh, Tapati. 2020. Kurmali Thar. In: Linguistic Survey of India: Bihar, pp. 439 ff. (phonology sec. 2, pp. 451-465). Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India.
sources.note: Silent on stress. p. 451: 'The Phonemic Inventory of Kurmali Thar comprises 36 segmental phonemes out of which 8 are vowels and 28 consonants. Nasalization is realized as a supra-segmental phoneme.' The 'Supra segmental Phoneme' subsection (p. 452-453) treats only nasalization; then vowel sequences, clusters, 2.7 syllables (open/closed, mono/di/polysyllabic).

sources.citation: Singh, H. N. 2017. Kurmali Vyakaran [कुरमाली व्याकरण / कुरमाली बेयाकरन]. Ranchi: Jharkhand Jharokha. ISBN 978-93-85595-21-9. In Kurmali (Devanagari). archive.org dli.language.1366; TOC and varna section (book pp. 1-9) scanned with tesseract hin+eng.
sources.note: Silent. Traditional school-grammar 'varna vichar' (letters, vowels hrasva/dirgha, consonant classes, Hindi-to-Kurmali sound correspondences such as y>j, v>b, cluster splitting); no term for stress/accent (बलाघात/स्वराघात) appears.

sources.note: Silent; the 'Pronunciation' paragraph (p. 147) covers only o>a (Bengali-style open o), a>e before i/e, prothetic h.
